indicators.name: Third-party payer funds purchase on behalf of a victim
indicators.desc: Incident response firm, broker or insurer funds crypto on behalf of a client, with unclear client identity or authorisation.

indicators.name: P2P advertiser with high volume and many unrelated counterparties
indicators.desc: Seller trades large volume with numerous buyers across payment methods and accounts, resembling unlicensed money transmission.

indicators.name: Vessel with history of AIS gaps or name and flag changes
indicators.desc: Vessel switches off position tracking, changes names or flags often and is on IUU lists.

indicators.name: Front businesses combining legal goods and wildlife products
indicators.desc: Import-export firm in furniture, traditional medicine or seafood with unusually high-value shipments or inconsistent product descriptions.

indicators.name: Recruited receiving account for reshipping or payment processing
indicators.desc: Mule-side: individuals recruited through job adverts receive and forward funds.

indicators.name: Receiving account is new or recently dormant with many unrelated senders
indicators.desc: Mule-side: a recently opened or reactivated account receives payments from many unrelated people with narratives that do not fit the stated profile.

indicators.name: Multiple prior scam alerts or repeat victimisation
indicators.desc: Victim-side: the customer previously reported or was warned of fraud and is again sending payments to new payees.

indicators.name: New account with immediate cheque deposits
indicators.desc: Account opened and quickly funded by cheques.

indicators.name: Thin or recently created credit file with high requested limits
indicators.desc: Synthetic: little history yet applications seek large lines or multiple facilities.

indicators.name: Straw buyer or nominee applicant
indicators.desc: Applicant's profile does not match purchase, with another party funding or controlling.

indicators.name: Undisclosed liabilities or multiple simultaneous applications
indicators.desc: Same borrower applies at several lenders before bureaux update.

indicators.name: Recently opened account receiving government payments
indicators.desc: New accounts used to receive claims.

indicators.name: New joint account holder or power of attorney added
indicators.desc: Access given to a new person shortly before unusual activity.

indicators.name: Frequent cash-in-transit use by a non-retail customer
indicators.desc: Cash collected or delivered without commercial need.

indicators.name: Individual or business holder lacks economic link to deposit areas
indicators.desc: Account holder profile shows no business or family ties in places where deposits occur.

indicators.name: Account opened with limited documentation or by recruited individuals
indicators.desc: Account holders include students, unemployed people or newcomers sharing similar addresses.

indicators.name: Client unwilling to provide ownership or source of funds
indicators.desc: Refuses details of beneficial owner or source.

indicators.name: Newly acquired PEP status not re-assessed
indicators.desc: Customer becomes PEP after onboarding without update.

indicators.name: Shipment volume exceeds the counterparty's capability
indicators.desc: Quantities or values are out of proportion to the size, history or industry of trading parties.

indicators.name: Introduced customers with no direct contact
indicators.desc: Client business introduced through TCSP with no face-to-face contact and little data.

indicators.name: Personal account used for business flows
indicators.desc: Business-like volumes in personal account.

indicators.name: Armed groups or militias as end users linked to customers
indicators.desc: Customer's counterparties are tied to armed groups.

indicators.name: Many small online storefronts with common bank accounts or directors
indicators.desc: Network of shops sharing accounts.

indicators.name: Pharmacy, clinic or online pharmacy with abnormal opioid volumes
indicators.desc: Dispensing, imports or payments exceeding peers for controlled substances.

indicators.name: Underground casino or card house with cash and chip sales
indicators.desc: Cash-heavy venue with transfers by chat apps.

indicators.name: Respondent bank with presence or business in jurisdictions of proliferation concern
indicators.desc: Respondent holds accounts or branches in higher-risk countries without strong controls.

indicators.name: Customer or counterparty business inconsistent with technical goods traded
indicators.desc: Trading or logistics firm with no technical background transacts in items with possible weapons or missile applications.

indicators.name: Customer in transit country suddenly trades controlled or high-priority items
indicators.desc: A firm with a different history begins importing restricted items for resale.

indicators.name: Inconsistent tax residency declarations
indicators.desc: Customer self-certifies residence in one jurisdiction while mailing address, phone, spending or travel point to another.

indicators.name: Minors or young adults funded by third parties
indicators.desc: Accounts of young customers receive small repeated funds from unrelated adults, followed by cash-out.

indicators.name: Operator account with transactions inconsistent with a retail remittance profile
indicators.desc: Business accounts of an MVTS or agent receive large pooled deposits and send bulk payments to a small set of foreign counterparties.

indicators.name: Operating-company profile with scam-infrastructure spending and no business footprint
indicators.desc: A corporate customer in recruitment, customer-service outsourcing, gaming, crypto or consultancy, often with remote principals, shows spending on bulk telecoms, servers, hosting, domains, devices and accommodation but little revenue, payroll or customer activity consistent with its stated business.

indicators.name: Vague invoices for unspecified services
indicators.desc: Invoices describe 'consulting', 'marketing support' or 'liaison services' without deliverables, timesheets or reports.

indicators.name: Frequent contract variations or change orders
indicators.desc: Scope and price rise significantly through repeated amendments shortly after award.

indicators.name: Emergency or single-source award with weak justification
indicators.desc: Use of urgency or sole-source exceptions for non-urgent purchases.

indicators.name: Remote onboarding with weak verification
indicators.desc: Onboarding relies on a single image or unverified selfie, with no database check.

indicators.name: Identity document tampering or forensic failure
indicators.desc: Identity document or selfie shows alteration, font or layout anomalies, or fails security-feature or forensic checks (including deepfake or injection artefacts).

indicators.name: Inconsistent personal details across documents or sources
indicators.desc: Names, dates of birth, addresses or national ID numbers differ between documents, bureaux or the application.

indicators.name: Fictitious or unverifiable address
indicators.desc: Address does not exist, is a mail drop, or fails verification against authoritative data.

indicators.name: Shared identifiers across unrelated customers
indicators.desc: Same phone, email, address, device or ID number appears across multiple unrelated customers or users.

indicators.name: Synthetic identity with thin or newly created footprint
indicators.desc: Thin or recently created credit and digital footprint, with mixed attributes suggesting a fabricated identity.

indicators.name: Documents or images reused or templated across applicants
indicators.desc: Same document image, selfie, template, font or background appears across different applicants or after rejection.

indicators.name: Expired, unusual or low-assurance documents
indicators.desc: Applicant offers documents of limited reliability or unusual types without explanation.

indicators.name: Applicant details match watchlist or fraud record
indicators.desc: Application data matches known fraud, mule or exited-customer records.

indicators.name: Signature or contact details differ on later instructions
indicators.desc: Later instructions carry signatures or contact details that depart from onboarding records.

indicators.name: Payee name verification fails or mismatches
indicators.desc: Names mismatch or accounts recently created for the payee.

indicators.name: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information
indicators.desc: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.

indicators.name: Selfie or video shows signs of synthetic or injected media
indicators.desc: Liveness checks reveal artefacts, virtual cameras or replayed streams.

indicators.name: Dates of birth, SSN or national ID not matching authoritative records
indicators.desc: Authoritative checks fail or show multiple identities on one number.

indicators.name: Project lacking verifiable registry entry or independent verification
indicators.desc: Credits sold from a project with no registry listing, uncertified verifier or conflicting documents.

indicators.name: Catch documentation inconsistent with vessel capacity or licence
indicators.desc: Landing volumes or species exceed capacity, quota or fishing area.

indicators.name: Trade documents inconsistent with each other
indicators.desc: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.

indicators.name: Unclear provenance of gold, metals or stones
indicators.desc: Gold, metals or stones lack licence, assay or chain-of-custody evidence of origin, or are claimed as recycled scrap.

indicators.name: Waste shipped as used goods or recyclables
indicators.desc: Containers described as used electronics, vehicles, plastics or metal scrap with signs of unsorted waste.

indicators.name: Trade in CITES-listed species with irregular permits
indicators.desc: Customer exports or imports listed species with permits that do not verify, repeat or conflict with quantities.

indicators.name: Transit via logistics hubs with changed consignee or false declarations
indicators.desc: Reconsignment or splits in transit with different declared contents.

indicators.name: Lookalike or recently registered sender domain
indicators.desc: Spoofed email domain or reply-to differs subtly from the genuine counterparty.

indicators.name: Invoice amount or format differs from prior invoices
indicators.desc: Victim-side: genuine-looking invoice has altered layout, round figures or inconsistent references.

indicators.name: Stated income or employer not verifiable
indicators.desc: Application cites employer or income that cannot be confirmed.

indicators.name: Cheque appears altered or counterfeit
indicators.desc: Image shows alterations, mismatched MICR or font.

indicators.name: Stolen mail cheque deposited under changed payee
indicators.desc: Payee name altered; account holder differs.

indicators.name: Inconsistent accounts of the incident
indicators.desc: Statements, evidence and photos do not match.

indicators.name: Application misrepresentation such as hidden drivers or addresses
indicators.desc: Details given at quote differ from actual use.

indicators.name: Income or employment documents show signs of alteration
indicators.desc: Payslips, tax forms or bank statements display template reuse or inconsistent fonts.

indicators.name: Property valuation materially above comparable sales
indicators.desc: Valuation inflated relative to recent transactions in the area.

indicators.name: Occupancy or purpose misrepresented
indicators.desc: Owner-occupier application where property is let or used differently.

indicators.name: Tenders show suspiciously similar pricing or documents
indicators.desc: Bids contain shared errors, formatting or pricing relationships.

indicators.name: Invoices for services or goods not received
indicators.desc: Payment is approved without delivery evidence.

indicators.name: Claim details inconsistent with income, residency or account history
indicators.desc: Declared income, dependants or circumstances conflict with data held on the customer.

indicators.name: Same invoice or shipment financed or invoiced multiple times
indicators.desc: The same invoice, bill of lading or goods are presented to multiple financiers or invoiced more than once.

indicators.name: Unusually low wages, deductions or accommodation charges
indicators.desc: Pay after deductions is far below minimum wage standards; heavy deductions for housing, food and transport.

indicators.name: Winnings claims lacking supporting records
indicators.desc: Requests for win certificates or cheques not matching records.

indicators.name: Customer lacks records of senders and recipients
indicators.desc: No ledger of clients, with limited or no identification.

indicators.name: Loan with no commercial purpose or unusual terms
indicators.desc: Interest-free, no repayments, or terms inconsistent with market.

indicators.name: Inconsistent loan documentation or backdated agreements
indicators.desc: Dates, signatures or amounts inconsistent.

indicators.name: Unregistered or unlicensed fundraising
indicators.desc: Raising funds without registration or authority.

indicators.name: Fake or inflated beneficiaries and invoices
indicators.desc: Payments to suppliers with weak evidence.

indicators.name: Generic or inconsistent business activity
indicators.desc: Vague business descriptions such as consulting or general trading; documents inconsistent with the activity.

indicators.name: Related-party or unknown-party loans and deposits lacking documentation
indicators.desc: Intercompany loans, director deposits or loans from unknown persons with no agreements, interest or repayment terms.

indicators.name: Fake commercial front using civilian goods descriptions
indicators.desc: Containers described as machinery or toys with weights conflicting with documents.

indicators.name: Provenance gaps or documents inconsistent with object history
indicators.desc: Missing ownership chain, 1970-era gap or fake certificates.

indicators.name: Vague or generic goods descriptions
indicators.desc: Trade documents use generic terms or imprecise descriptions or mismatched HS codes where specifics would be expected.

indicators.name: Forced purchase of services, supplies or cars at inflated prices
indicators.desc: Businesses pay inflated invoices to specific suppliers.

indicators.name: Goods in transit declared to low-tax or non-EU destinations but not arriving
indicators.desc: Duty-suspended shipments disappear or end up in domestic markets.

indicators.name: Use of multiple identities or fabricated credentials in onboarding
indicators.desc: Documents, employment history or references show signs of fabrication.

indicators.name: End-user information vague, missing or refused
indicators.desc: Customer or buyer is evasive about end use, final destination or end-user certificate, or declines re-export undertakings.

indicators.name: Price or specification not in line with commercial norms
indicators.desc: Equipment priced far above or below market, or specifications altered to fall below control thresholds.

indicators.name: Vessel identity discrepancies
indicators.desc: Physical details, IMO or name do not match registry records, or signs of identity spoofing.

indicators.name: Insurance, classification or P&I cover absent or changed abruptly
indicators.desc: Cover is cancelled, provided by unknown insurers or classification society changes.

indicators.name: Letter of credit terms that are unusually flexible or amended repeatedly
indicators.desc: Frequent amendments to beneficiary, destination or description, or acceptance of discrepant documents.

indicators.name: Vessel, voyage or shipper details missing or implausible
indicators.desc: Transport documents lack vessel identifiers or show impossible voyage timing.

indicators.name: Goods relabelled, repackaged or invoiced under different HS codes
indicators.desc: Descriptions change between stages of the supply chain.

indicators.name: Document or sanction-licence irregularities
indicators.desc: Applications or licence reliance appear inconsistent or altered.

indicators.name: Attestations of price compliance without supporting invoices
indicators.desc: Counterparties provide generic declarations but cannot supply itemised contracts and invoices showing the price of oil and services.

indicators.name: Discrepancy between loading port, origin documents and tracking
indicators.desc: Declared origin differs from vessel tracking and port records.

indicators.name: Free-text fields containing instructions to avoid mention of certain parties
indicators.desc: Messages instruct downstream banks not to reference parties or contain unusual remarks.

indicators.name: Different party name between message and underlying invoice
indicators.desc: Payment shows one remitter while documents show another.

indicators.name: Invoices with identical formats across 'unrelated' suppliers
indicators.desc: Documents share templates, wording or bank accounts across different companies.

indicators.name: Local taxation language in invoices or payments
indicators.desc: Documents reference levies, tolls or taxes payable to non-state bodies or local commanders.

indicators.name: Early-access or hardship claim without supporting evidence
indicators.desc: Request to release retirement funds before the normal age on grounds such as ill health, hardship or emigration where the supporting evidence is thin, inconsistent or unverifiable.

indicators.name: Claim with no commercial basis or prior trading history
indicators.desc: The legal claim rests on a contract, service or loss that lacks supporting commercial evidence, a trading history between the parties, or a plausible amount in relation to the stated losses.

indicators.name: Loads immediately followed by foreign ATM withdrawals
indicators.desc: Funds are drawn down in cash overseas or in high-risk locations soon after loading.

indicators.name: Funds routed to project developers in high-risk jurisdictions with no activity
indicators.desc: Payments to developers in remote regions without site evidence.

indicators.name: Port calls in ports of low inspection standards
indicators.desc: Frequent landings at ports with weak controls or non-parties to port state measures.

indicators.name: Origin country is a transit-only processor with no forests
indicators.desc: Exports declared from a country with little domestic timber supply, indicating laundering of origin.

indicators.name: Operation in or adjacent to protected areas or indigenous lands
indicators.desc: Customer's supply is sourced from areas with legal restrictions or conflicts reported.

indicators.name: Armed-group territory or sanctioned parties in conflict areas
indicators.desc: Trade, production or payments involve territories controlled by armed groups or parties linked to them.

indicators.name: Shipments to countries with weak controls and few recycling facilities
indicators.desc: Exports to destinations known as dumping sites.

indicators.name: Wildlife-related payments between source, transit and consumer countries
indicators.desc: Flows between countries known as supply, transit and demand points linked to a small business.

indicators.name: Payments to money transfer services overseas
indicators.desc: Money services used for ad hoc transfers to unknown beneficiaries.

indicators.name: First payment to a new beneficiary in a different jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Victim-side: payment to a new account, often foreign, unrelated to the supplier's usual country.

indicators.name: Address is mail-drop, virtual or shared by many applicants
indicators.desc: Multiple unrelated applicants share an address with no occupancy history.

indicators.name: Suppliers in sectors or regions with high forced-labour risk
indicators.desc: Sourcing from sectors such as agriculture, fishing, garments or mining in regions flagged by credible reports.

indicators.name: Accounts or flows in border regions with cross-border movement
indicators.desc: Accounts in border or transit areas show frequent deposits with matching cross-border transfers or rapid withdrawals.

indicators.name: Cash deposits from many states or regions
indicators.desc: Account receives cash deposits across geographically distant locations from the account holder's home area.

indicators.name: Funds sent offshore soon after collection
indicators.desc: Aggregated funds are wired or sent through remittance to foreign jurisdictions.

indicators.name: Customer geography far from the professional's practice
indicators.desc: No reason to use this adviser.

indicators.name: Funds return from offshore as foreign investment
indicators.desc: Money sent abroad reappears as shareholder investment or loan.

indicators.name: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls
indicators.desc: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.

indicators.name: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods
indicators.desc: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.

indicators.name: Shipping through high-risk transit hubs with changed destinations
indicators.desc: Arms shipments change consignee or route.

indicators.name: Objects from conflict zones or countries with looting
indicators.desc: Antiquities exported from affected regions with new papers.

indicators.name: Shipments transiting free zones and repackaged
indicators.desc: Goods relabelled in transit hubs.

indicators.name: Businesses closing or reporting threats alongside payment spikes
indicators.desc: Sector-wide complaints in area linked to payments.

indicators.name: Payments to or from free-trade zones and tax-free ports
indicators.desc: Transfers linked to zones known for tobacco diversion.

indicators.name: Port calls at locations of concern followed by false next port
indicators.desc: Vessel declares destinations inconsistent with subsequent movements.

indicators.name: Access from sanctioned jurisdictions via VPN or proxy
indicators.desc: Technical indicators suggest the user is located in a comprehensively sanctioned area.

indicators.name: Delivery to forwarder, mailbox or address unrelated to buyer
indicators.desc: Goods or cards are shipped to freight forwarders, reshippers, mail drops or addresses with no storage or sales operations or link to the buyer.

indicators.name: Sharp rise in exports to specific transit countries of restricted items
indicators.desc: Aggregate trade data shows spikes in categories of concern to particular countries.

indicators.name: Provider acts for many clients from the same higher-risk jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Concentration of high-risk clients.

indicators.name: Payments routed through banks in jurisdictions with weak controls for no clear reason
indicators.desc: Routing does not follow normal correspondent paths.

indicators.name: Cash or card use in border and transit areas near conflict zones
indicators.desc: Cash withdrawals, ATM or card use occur at transit points or border regions near conflict zones.

indicators.name: Transfers following threat or abduction reports from region
indicators.desc: Payments from relatives or employers rise coincident with publicly reported kidnappings or extortion campaigns.

indicators.name: Travel and accommodation spending to conflict-adjacent regions
indicators.desc: Spending on flights, border-area hotels or overland transport near conflict zones inconsistent with known occupation or history.

indicators.name: Customer location inconsistent with declared residence
indicators.desc: IP or device signals suggest access from conflict-adjacent regions while KYC indicates elsewhere.

indicators.name: Transfers to jurisdictions with weak transparency soon after reporting changes
indicators.desc: Funds shifted to non-participating or low-transparency jurisdictions around the introduction of reporting obligations or voluntary-disclosure windows.

indicators.name: Nexus to FATF black-listed jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Customer, owner or counterparty is connected to a jurisdiction subject to a FATF call for action.

indicators.name: Nexus to FATF grey-listed jurisdiction
indicators.desc: Connection to a jurisdiction under increased monitoring for strategic deficiencies.

indicators.name: Secrecy or low-transparency jurisdiction nexus
indicators.desc: Entities, accounts or assets are booked in jurisdictions offering strong secrecy or limited transparency, including where unrelated to the entity's operations.

indicators.name: Conflict zone or fragile state exposure
indicators.desc: Activity involves regions with armed conflict, weak governance or active terrorist groups.

indicators.name: High-corruption jurisdiction nexus
indicators.desc: Funds or wealth are linked to or transferred to and from jurisdictions with high perceived corruption.

indicators.name: Routing through trade-diversion or transshipment hubs
indicators.desc: Goods or payments route through third-country hubs or ports with no commercial rationale, or hubs known for rerouting.

indicators.name: Sanctioned country proximity
indicators.desc: Customer or flows are located in or adjacent to comprehensively sanctioned areas.

indicators.name: Offshore financial centre use for non-resident clients
indicators.desc: Funds booked or routed via offshore centres with minimal client ties.

indicators.name: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies
indicators.desc: Payments use corridors identified in typology reports as high risk, including regions where informal value transfer is prevalent.

indicators.name: Nominee directors or shareholders
indicators.desc: Registered directors or shareholders appear to act for undisclosed principals, serve many entities or have no real decision-making role.

indicators.name: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale
indicators.desc: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.

indicators.name: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle
indicators.desc: Property, art, vessels or other valuables are acquired or held via a company, trust or storage arrangement with concealed beneficial owners.

indicators.name: Passive offshore vehicle or foundation holding personal assets
indicators.desc: A foundation, shell or similar vehicle in a low-transparency jurisdiction holds an individual's investments, property or accounts without commercial purpose.

indicators.name: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified
indicators.desc: Ownership or governance is opaque and no natural person who owns or controls the entity can be identified after reasonable effort.

indicators.name: Shell entity with no operating footprint
indicators.desc: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.

indicators.name: Newly formed entity with vague purpose and large flows
indicators.desc: Recently incorporated entity or group of entities with generic business descriptions shows significant turnover or purchases soon after formation.

indicators.name: Registered address shared by many entities
indicators.desc: Customer shares a registered address, mailbox, agent or phone with numerous unrelated companies, such as a mass-registration or virtual office.

indicators.name: Short-lived or rotating entities with common controllers
indicators.desc: Entities are repeatedly formed, abandoned or replaced by successors sharing directors, addresses or history of prior defaulted companies.

indicators.name: Multiple entities under common control
indicators.desc: Several apparently separate businesses or sub-accounts share owners, signatories, addresses, devices or bank accounts.

indicators.name: Ownership or controllers linked to designated or previously reported parties
indicators.desc: Owners, officers or associates match sanctions or designation lists, prior suspicious reports or adverse media.

indicators.name: Joint-venture partner owned by government-connected persons
indicators.desc: Local partner's owners include officials or relatives without disclosure or fair valuation of their contribution.

indicators.name: Supplier lacks capacity for awarded contract
indicators.desc: Awardee has no relevant staff, assets or experience and subcontracts nearly all work.

indicators.name: Safe deposit boxes

indicators.desc: Trade in antiquities or artefacts with gaps in provenance linked to conflict-zone origin.

indicators.desc: Incoming funds are quickly sent abroad or converted to virtual assets soon after being credited.

indicators.name: Transfers to many newly created crypto addresses
indicators.desc: Repeated small or fixed-amount transfers to many fresh or new crypto addresses.

indicators.name: Cash deposits just below reporting or identification threshold
indicators.desc: Repeated cash deposits kept just under a reporting, identification or monitoring threshold.

indicators.name: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts

indicators.name: Non-cash transfers or loads just below identification or reporting thresholds
indicators.desc: Repeated transfers, remittances or card/wallet loads kept just below an identification, record-keeping or travel-rule threshold.

indicators.name: Payments or claims split to stay below internal approval limits
indicators.desc: Payments, claims or contracts are broken into amounts just under internal authorisation limits.

indicators.name: Repeated round-value transactions
indicators.desc: Transactions are repeatedly in round or unusually uniform amounts that do not fit the stated purpose.

indicators.name: Dormant account suddenly reactivated or high-velocity activity
indicators.desc: A dormant or low-activity account suddenly shows high-velocity inflows and outflows.

indicators.name: Sudden large increase in transaction volume
indicators.desc: Transaction volume or value rises abruptly well beyond historical levels, including through a respondent or reactivated account.

indicators.name: Activity inconsistent with customer profile

indicators.name: Volumes exceed documented production or capacity
indicators.desc: Exports or output reported exceed documented production, concession or capacity limits.

indicators.name: Circular or round-trip flows among related parties
indicators.desc: Funds or goods-linked payments loop back to the originator or between related counterparties, or are traded back and forth.

indicators.name: Mirror or offsetting transactions between jurisdictions
indicators.desc: Reciprocal or offsetting payments occur between counterparties or operators in different countries with no direct value transfer.

indicators.name: Workers paid to third-party or multiple accounts
indicators.desc: Wages are paid to accounts not held by the worker or split across several accounts.

indicators.name: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after receipt
indicators.desc: Virtual assets are moved across chains or bridges and converted soon after being received.

indicators.name: Refund and chargeback abuse
indicators.desc: Unusual refund or chargeback volumes or cycles relative to sales.

indicators.name: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.desc: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.

indicators.name: High-value purchases paid in cash, crypto or non-standard funds

indicators.desc: Large or repeated cash payments to informal traders, producers or workers in extraction or supply chains.

indicators.desc: Payments are made by parties with no apparent link to the underlying transaction, goods or services.

indicators.name: Sudden liquidation of savings or assets
indicators.desc: Savings, investments or assets are sold abruptly, followed by withdrawal or transfer.

indicators.name: Sudden credit utilisation spike then bust-out
indicators.desc: Credit builds up and is then rapidly utilised to limit or cashed out after a period of low use.

indicators.name: Large buy-in or deposits with little underlying activity
indicators.desc: Substantial funds are deposited or bought in with minimal gambling or betting activity before withdrawal.

indicators.name: Fee or tax payment demanded to release funds
indicators.desc: Payments are made as fees or taxes supposedly needed to release a prize, loan, inheritance or gains.

indicators.name: Payment references suggesting scam scripts

indicators.name: Rapid onward movement after cash credits
indicators.desc: Cash deposited is quickly withdrawn or transferred onward, including to another location or to unhosted wallets.

indicators.name: Large credit followed by prompt withdrawals
indicators.desc: A cheque deposit or refund is credited and quickly withdrawn or transferred before it clears or is verified.

indicators.name: Rapid stored-value or wallet hops then cash-out
indicators.desc: Stored value or funds move quickly between wallets or cards and are then cashed out.

indicators.name: Bulk purchase or sale of cards or vouchers
indicators.desc: Large volumes of prepaid cards or gift cards are purchased or sold.

indicators.name: Cash or anonymous donations
indicators.desc: Donations are made through cash, anonymous collections or structured amounts.

indicators.name: Professional client account used as pass-through
indicators.desc: A professional's client account is used to move funds with no underlying legal or advisory work.

indicators.name: Recurring small cash payments to border, customs or permit agents
indicators.desc: Repeated low-value cash disbursements or petty cash entries labelled 'expediting', 'facilitation' or 'processing' at ports, borders or ministries.

indicators.name: Fees to distributors well above market margin
indicators.desc: Distributor discounts or rebates are unusually large without commercial rationale, leaving room for onward payments.

indicators.desc: Winning supplier transfers funds to persons or companies connected to the procuring official shortly after payment.

indicators.desc: Funds from government bodies or state enterprises arrive at private or personal accounts with no apparent contractual basis.

indicators.name: Rapid movement through correspondent or private banking channels
indicators.desc: Large sums move quickly through several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, with no hold period.

indicators.name: Cash from bulk notes in poor condition or unusual denominations
indicators.desc: Large volumes of small or bundled notes deposited in sequence.

indicators.desc: Creator mints and sells quickly to a single buyer funded by a cluster with no history.

indicators.name: Payments for at-sea transhipment, fuel and supplies

indicators.name: Repeated payments to same beneficiary with escalating narratives

indicators.name: Rapid payments from third-party or overdrawn accounts to inflate limits

indicators.desc: Fees or deposits in cash.

indicators.name: Large cash deposits followed by payments to many individuals or businesses
indicators.desc: Cash received and paid out to numerous parties abroad or locally.

indicators.name: Overfunded policies and partial withdrawals

indicators.desc: Shares deposited and moved with no market activity.

indicators.name: Loan funded by related offshore party and repaid early
indicators.desc: Borrower receives loan from an entity linked to themselves and repays rapidly.

indicators.name: Loan secured on assets or deposits from third parties of unclear origin
indicators.desc: Collateral is cash deposit or asset funded by unknown source.

indicators.name: Unusual real-estate or luxury purchases
indicators.desc: High-value purchases by PEPs or associates abroad.

indicators.name: Funds move in fixed commission-like deductions
indicators.desc: Recurring small percentage retained from inbound flows consistent with fee-taking by an intermediary.

indicators.name: Mortgage repaid early or from unusual sources
indicators.desc: Loan quickly settled in lump sum or by third parties.

indicators.name: Illicit and legitimate funds mixed in operating account
indicators.desc: Business income blended with unexplained inflows.

indicators.name: Frequent payments to the same third-party beneficiary of unclear purpose
indicators.desc: Recurring payments to unexplained counterparties.

indicators.name: Multiple firearm or component purchases by one person for others
indicators.desc: Repeated purchases of guns, parts or ammunition inconsistent with sport use, paid by different people.

indicators.name: Cash purchases with prompt resale or export
indicators.desc: Weapons purchased for cash and quickly moved abroad.

indicators.name: Payments to manufacturers in known counterfeit production regions with no brand
indicators.desc: Payments to factories lacking licences.

indicators.name: Cash-out through gift cards, prepaid, or money mules in other countries
indicators.desc: Funds converted into hard-to-trace instruments.

indicators.name: Regular fixed payments from a small business to an individual with no invoices
indicators.desc: Payments at regular intervals to a person or company with no service provided.

indicators.name: High-interest informal loans with repayments to non-lender individuals
indicators.desc: Repeated payments with high effective interest rates and rollovers.

indicators.name: Wholesaler purchases far exceed local market demand
indicators.desc: Volumes of cigarettes or alcohol bought by a retailer or distributor exceed plausible consumption.

indicators.name: Cross-border cash and remittance flows from retailers to overseas suppliers
indicators.desc: Regular remittances to suppliers in source countries without invoices.

indicators.name: Payments that include references to designated or restricted entities
indicators.desc: Payment messages show names, addresses or vessels linked to restricted lists.

indicators.name: Open-account trade with buyers in high-risk jurisdictions lacking track record
indicators.desc: New relationships with large unsecured trade flows to or from countries of proliferation concern.

indicators.name: Large OTC or peer-to-peer purchases paid in cash or non-bank rails
indicators.desc: Purchases with limited traceability to source of funds.

indicators.name: Stablecoin use to hold value of designated person's funds
indicators.desc: Large stablecoin balances held with limited stated purpose by customers linked to designated persons.

indicators.name: Payments from jurisdictions of concern in settlement of third-country sales
indicators.desc: Funds arrive from or return to parties in the restricted jurisdiction.

indicators.name: Multiple small shipments to avoid scrutiny
indicators.desc: Orders split into smaller consignments to stay below review thresholds.

indicators.name: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.desc: Unusually high or opaque fees.

indicators.name: Asset transfers shortly before or after designation
indicators.desc: Titles move to relatives, trusts or associates around designation dates.

indicators.name: Cargo priced near cap with inflated freight, insurance or ancillary charges
indicators.desc: Separately invoiced services carry unusually high costs.

indicators.name: Payments in alternative currencies or via smaller banks
indicators.desc: Payments denominated or routed to avoid mainstream channels.

indicators.name: Funding of a company by a designated person's connected sources
indicators.desc: Capital injections, loans or guarantees come from entities linked to a designated party.

indicators.name: Use of cover payments that omit underlying parties
indicators.desc: Cover message shows only the banks, with details of ultimate parties absent.

indicators.name: Funds repatriated via cash, bearer instruments or third-party accounts
indicators.desc: Customer deposits foreign-sourced cash or cheques or receives funds from unrelated individuals, avoiding visible foreign accounts.

indicators.name: Cash withdrawals match payroll amounts
indicators.desc: Large cash withdrawals shortly after receiving client funds, close to total weekly wages, with no matching payroll tax payments.

indicators.name: Payments to workers just under tax or reporting thresholds
indicators.desc: Pay split into amounts staying below withholding or reporting thresholds.

indicators.name: Declared turnover lower than card and bank takings imply
indicators.desc: Card acquiring volumes or supplier purchases suggest higher sales than the business reports to authorities.

indicators.name: Cash deposits well below expected for business type
indicators.desc: A business with high card use but little cash banking, despite sector norms of cash trade.

indicators.name: Payments in and out the same day with thin margin
indicators.desc: Funds received from buyer are paid onward to supplier, often same day, leaving little retained.

indicators.name: Many small donations from geographically diverse donors to a single organiser
indicators.desc: Large numbers of low-value contributions from many countries into one recipient account that then withdraws promptly.

indicators.name: Urgent transfers described as emergency family or legal payments
indicators.desc: Customer receives or sends sudden large transfers framed as emergencies, to unfamiliar parties or accounts abroad.

indicators.name: Cash collected from multiple unrelated individuals then moved abroad
indicators.desc: Collection of funds across diaspora members or business owners followed by consolidated cross-border transfer.

indicators.name: Remittances from family or associates to individuals in border areas
indicators.desc: Recurrent small transfers to recipients in or near conflict zones with no clear family relationship or humanitarian need.

indicators.name: Loans or credit taken with no repayment intent
indicators.desc: Customer obtains borrowing and then leaves the jurisdiction, defaulting.

indicators.name: Travel booked to destination near conflict via indirect route
indicators.desc: Itineraries with unusual routing, one-way tickets and short-notice booking inconsistent with customer profile.

indicators.name: Settlement via trade, with mismatched invoices
indicators.desc: Offsetting flows are arranged through trade payments unrelated to the underlying goods.

indicators.name: Rapid consumer credit drawdown with no stated purpose
indicators.desc: Customer takes several unsecured loans, credit cards or overdraft limits in a short window and withdraws or transfers the proceeds quickly, then ceases repayment.

indicators.name: Payments to intermediaries in neighbouring transit jurisdictions
indicators.desc: Commodity proceeds are settled through agents or companies in jurisdictions adjacent to conflict areas and then forwarded onward.

indicators.name: Unusual use of cash or barter in commodity deals
indicators.desc: Settlement via cash, barter or netting arrangements without documentation.

indicators.name: Rapid conversion of donations to stablecoins then off-ramp through peer-to-peer channels
indicators.desc: Funds are converted and cashed out using unregulated peer-to-peer exchanges.

indicators.name: Sudden large inflows from newly funded unhosted wallets
indicators.desc: Large first deposits from unhosted wallets with no history, followed by immediate transfers out.

indicators.name: Rapid chain of transfers between retirement schemes or providers
indicators.desc: A retirement balance moves through several schemes, providers or trustees in a short period without a stated reason, often ending in an account or product with weaker oversight.

indicators.name: Settlement or award funded by a party with no link to the dispute
indicators.desc: The payment of a settlement or judgment comes from an unrelated third party, a newly created entity or an offshore account instead of the named respondent.

indicators.name: Orders placed and cancelled without intent to execute
indicators.desc: Large orders are repeatedly entered and withdrawn before execution, or small orders are layered, in a way that moves the visible price or depth in favour of positions held elsewhere.

indicators.name: Year-end or retrospective price adjustments between related parties
indicators.desc: Large true-up, credit-note or compensating payments between group companies at period end that bring profit into line with a target outcome rather than with underlying activity.

indicators.name: Manual entries through internal or suspense accounts hiding customer flows
indicators.desc: Funds move via manual journals, suspense, clearing or staff-controlled internal accounts, so customer-level records do not show the real origin, destination or beneficial party.

indicators.name: Same external wallet used by multiple unrelated customers
indicators.desc: Many different customers send to or whitelist the same external address.

indicators.name: Destination wallet linked to scam or fraud clusters
indicators.desc: Receiving address is attributed to investment, romance or impersonation scams.

indicators.name: Operator lacks effective transaction monitoring
indicators.desc: Operator fails to monitor wallets, refunds or complaints, allowing patterns to persist.

indicators.name: Direct exposure to known darknet market addresses
indicators.desc: Customer deposits or withdrawals have direct or near-direct exposure to addresses attributed to darknet markets or their escrow wallets.

indicators.name: Use of mixers, privacy coins or privacy pools around platform activity
indicators.desc: Funds pass through mixers, privacy coins or privacy-preserving pools before or after platform activity without commercial rationale.

indicators.name: Payments for postage, packaging or related services alongside crypto activity
indicators.desc: Card and bank transactions to shipping supplies and anonymous mailbox services coincide with virtual asset sales or purchases.

indicators.name: Law-enforcement or media notice naming customer or wallet
indicators.desc: Third-party intelligence links the customer or addresses to marketplace activity.

indicators.name: Inbound funds traced to exploited protocols or hacks
indicators.desc: Deposits have provenance in a smart-contract exploit, bridge hack or theft attributed by analytics providers.

indicators.name: Interaction with sanctioned or designated contracts, mixers or addresses
indicators.desc: Transfers touch contracts, pools, relayers or addresses designated by authorities or flagged in advisories.

indicators.name: Collusive purchases between related buyer and seller accounts
indicators.desc: Accounts sharing devices or funding sources transact with each other to create revenue.

indicators.name: Buyers directed off-platform to pay
indicators.desc: Messaging encourages payment via transfer or crypto outside platform protections.

indicators.name: Deposits with direct or indirect exposure to mixing services
indicators.desc: Incoming virtual asset transfers trace to known mixer or tumbler clusters within a small number of hops.

indicators.name: Unlicensed or unregistered operator behaviour
indicators.desc: Individuals operate collection points or chat-app based services with no licence.

indicators.name: Wash or matched trades between connected parties
indicators.desc: Assets or securities are traded repeatedly between linked accounts or wallets at unrealistic prices.

indicators.name: Accounts bought with stolen cards then items resold
indicators.desc: Chargebacks on purchases of currency or items followed by transfer to other accounts.

indicators.name: Transaction descriptors or products inconsistent with registered business
indicators.desc: Card data show goods or services unrelated to the merchant's declared activity or website.

indicators.name: Use of multiple shell merchant accounts to spread volume
indicators.desc: Volumes distributed across many accounts to stay below monitoring thresholds.

indicators.name: Tops-up with fraudulent funding sources
indicators.desc: Loads via cards or accounts reported stolen, followed by cash-out.

indicators.name: Wallet attributed to ransomware or theft actors
indicators.desc: Source or destination address is attributed to ransomware affiliates, theft or designated actors.

indicators.name: Unhosted wallet with high-risk counterparties in history
indicators.desc: Self-hosted address has prior exposure to illicit services, scams or sanctioned addresses.

indicators.name: Inflated baseline or additionality claims
indicators.desc: Reduction claims implausible versus public data or comparable projects.

indicators.name: Mercury, cyanide and equipment purchases without mining licence
indicators.desc: Purchase of dredges, mercury or bulk chemicals by unlicensed persons.

indicators.name: Scam web domains or phone numbers reported
indicators.desc: External intelligence indicates active campaigns.

indicators.name: Mass of near-identical SMS or links referencing parcels or fines
indicators.desc: Bank brand impersonation campaigns observed in threat feeds and customer reports.

indicators.name: Claim shortly after policy inception or increase in cover
indicators.desc: Loss occurs soon after purchase or upgrade of cover.

indicators.name: Staged or contrived accident indicators
indicators.desc: Low-impact incidents with multiple occupants, witness and similar circumstances.

indicators.name: Ghost employee or duplicate bank account on payroll
indicators.desc: Payroll records show employees without HR evidence or shared bank details.

indicators.name: Promised returns far above market with low stated risk
indicators.desc: Operator marketing guarantees consistently high returns, often with testimonials and urgency; victims relay these claims when transferring.

indicators.name: Cash concealed in vehicles, shipments or parcels
indicators.desc: Cash found hidden in goods, freight or mail.

indicators.name: Business type inconsistent with location or customer base
indicators.desc: Cash business operating where demand appears limited, with few visible customers or irregular hours.

indicators.name: Junket or VIP operators moving funds across borders
indicators.desc: Junket arrangements shift large funds without clear play.

indicators.name: Player collusion or chip-dumping
indicators.desc: Players lose deliberately to a counterpart.

indicators.name: Professional's role unusual for the work
indicators.desc: Professional acts as nominee, director, or intermediary beyond normal remit.

indicators.name: Settlement via trade, invoices or gold
indicators.desc: Balancing between brokers is done through goods, invoices or precious metals.

indicators.name: Vehicle purchased for cash and exported quickly
indicators.desc: Luxury cars bought and shipped abroad soon after.

indicators.name: Circular trade or invoices among connected entities
indicators.desc: Invoices cycled among related firms, returning funds to origin.

indicators.name: Activities do not match stated objects
indicators.desc: Spending outside charitable purposes.

indicators.name: Complex use of multiple services for single flow
indicators.desc: One flow touches cash, remitters, trade invoices, crypto and corporate accounts in a short time.

indicators.name: Currency denomination or condition anomalies
indicators.desc: Cash arrives in unusual bundles, rubber-banded small notes, or mixed denominations inconsistent with the stated source.

indicators.name: Phantom shipment indicators
indicators.desc: No verifiable movement of goods: missing tracking, inspection or insurance evidence.

indicators.name: Bulk company formation for undisclosed clients
indicators.desc: TCSP forms large numbers of entities with little client information.

indicators.name: Counterfeit pharmaceuticals or safety-critical parts
indicators.desc: Medicines or auto parts from unlicensed sources.

indicators.name: Unusual betting patterns on lower-league or youth matches
indicators.desc: Large late stakes on obscure markets.

indicators.name: Nested relationships with unidentified downstream banks
indicators.desc: Respondent processes payments for other banks without disclosure.

indicators.name: Trade-related payments through correspondent for goods of proliferation concern
indicators.desc: Payments relate to goods on control lists or to parties on alerts.

indicators.name: Orders for items matching procurement watch lists or inquiries
indicators.desc: Goods, parties or addresses match published alerts by export-control or enforcement authorities.

indicators.name: AIS gaps in sensitive areas
indicators.desc: Vessel stops transmitting position data for extended periods near ports or transhipment areas of concern.

indicators.name: Frequent flag changes or flagging in registries with weak oversight
indicators.desc: Short intervals between flag changes or use of open registries with poor enforcement.

indicators.name: Ship-to-ship transfers without clear commercial purpose
indicators.desc: Vessel meets others at sea off normal transfer areas, followed by a changed declared destination.

indicators.name: Vessel or aircraft registered under flags of convenience with managers in secrecy locations
indicators.desc: Registration choices obscure the true owner.

indicators.name: Tanker with older age, unusual classification, or no recognised P&I

indicators.name: Screening alerts closed repeatedly for the same pattern with minimal rationale

indicators.name: Goods are high-value, low-weight and easily moved
indicators.desc: Trade in mobile phones, chips, precious metals, or CO2 allowances with no storage or transport evidence.

indicators.desc: Fundraising page, post or channel references violent groups, glorifies violence or is linked to accounts removed for extremism.
