indicators.desc: Operators in conflict-affected areas make periodic payments to individuals labelled as security, fees or consultants.

indicators.name: Purchase of equipment commonly carried by fighters
indicators.desc: Retail purchases of outdoor, protective, communication or medical gear in unusual quantity shortly before travel.

indicators.name: Purchases consistent with attack preparation reported by authorities
indicators.desc: Spending on items or services that match typologies shared by law enforcement or public-private partnerships, such as particular combinations of retail goods, vehicle hire and reconnaissance-type travel.

indicators.name: Operations in high-risk areas without credible delivery evidence
indicators.desc: Organisation sends funds to areas with active terrorist presence but cannot evidence projects, beneficiaries, partners or auditable delivery.

indicators.name: Funding flows following government transfers to non-state entities
indicators.desc: Payments from state or quasi-state entities to private firms or individuals lacking evident services.

indicators.name: Solicitation of donations via social channels using addresses linked to extremist content
indicators.desc: Publicly advertised wallet addresses appear in extremist channels or campaigns.

indicators.name: Payments by relatives for release or "fees" for a person held abroad
indicators.desc: Customers, often family members, send urgent payments abroad described as fees, fines or bail to secure the release of a relative who travelled for work, sometimes to many different recipient accounts or wallets.

indicators.name: Stored goods change title or are revalued repeatedly with no physical movement
indicators.desc: Ownership of goods held in secure storage passes between parties, or declared value changes sharply on entry, exit or transfer, while the items stay in place.

indicators.name: Image-rights or endorsement income paid to a third-country entity instead of the athlete
indicators.desc: Earnings from endorsement, image or commercial rights are directed to a company or account in a jurisdiction unconnected to the athlete or the paying party, with no clear contractual basis.

indicators.name: Sponsorship or naming-rights spend with no measurable promotional deliverables
indicators.desc: A sponsor pays substantial amounts to a sports body, club or event but there is little evidence of advertising, activation or audience reach, or the sponsor has no relevant business.

indicators.name: Trading ahead of material non-public announcements
indicators.desc: A customer or linked accounts take unusually large or well-timed positions shortly before a price-sensitive event such as a takeover, results release or listing decision, then close out soon after the news.

indicators.name: Promotion campaign alongside concentrated selling by connected holders
indicators.desc: Coordinated social-media, messaging-group or cold-call promotion of a low-priced instrument coincides with unusual buying volume while a small group of connected holders sells into the rise.

indicators.name: Token deployer or insider wallets distributing holdings into promoted price rise
indicators.desc: Wallets linked to a token's creator, early allocation or liquidity pool move large balances to exchanges or fresh wallets as promotion drives the price up, often followed by liquidity removal.

indicators.name: Royalty, licence or intangible-asset payments concentrated in a low-tax affiliate with minimal functions
indicators.desc: Recurring payments for brands, software or intellectual property go to a related entity in a low-tax jurisdiction that has little staff, development activity or control over the asset.

controls.name: Device intelligence and fingerprinting
controls.desc: Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.

controls.name: Behavioural biometrics and session analytics
controls.desc: Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.
aka: Remote access and login anomaly detection

controls.name: IP, geolocation and anonymisation detection
controls.desc: Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.

controls.name: Cash acceptance and settlement limits
controls.desc: Prohibits or caps cash for purchases, loans, donations and settlement above a set value, requiring documented non-cash methods and threshold reporting for dealers. It removes a low-traceability payment route.

controls.name: Cash exchange, declaration and courier checks
controls.desc: Collects identification for cash exchange, cross-checks cross-border cash declarations, screens freight, mail and cash-in-transit use and applies courier intelligence. It addresses bulk cash movement across borders.

controls.name: Cash deposit profiling and peer benchmarking
controls.desc: Compares cash deposits and withdrawals with expected activity, sector and location peers and declared turnover, alerting on outliers. It helps find cash that is inconsistent with the stated business.

controls.name: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
controls.desc: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.

controls.name: Electronic identity verification with liveness
controls.desc: Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.
aka: Stronger identity verification for remote workers

controls.name: Identity and supporting document authentication
controls.desc: Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

controls.name: Address and registered-office verification
controls.desc: Validates a stated address against postal or reference data, requires recent independent proof of residence or premises, and flags known mass-registration or virtual-office addresses. It supports identity assurance and helps reveal fictitious or shared addresses.

controls.name: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
controls.desc: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.

controls.name: Beneficial ownership identification and verification
controls.desc: Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

controls.name: Beneficial ownership information gate
controls.desc: Prevents account opening or activity until ownership and control information is provided and verified, with refusals escalated to compliance and unresolved cases handled under a defined policy. It stops relationships starting on withheld or unresolved ownership.

controls.name: Nominee and bearer instrument controls
controls.desc: Requires nominee shareholders, directors and signatories to declare their status and name the person they act for, and declines or immobilises bearer instruments. It limits the use of nominees and bearer forms to conceal the real controller.
aka: Certification of holder at each event

controls.name: Complex structure rationale and approval
controls.desc: Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.

controls.name: Trust and legal arrangement due diligence
controls.desc: Identifies all parties to a trust or similar arrangement, including settlor, trustees, protector and beneficiaries, and reviews the governing document for unusual control or reserved powers. It makes the controlling persons behind such vehicles visible.

controls.name: Substance and physical presence verification
controls.desc: Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

controls.name: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
controls.desc: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

controls.name: Source of funds verification
controls.desc: Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.
aka: Source of funds and wealth verification

controls.name: Source of wealth corroboration
controls.desc: Establishes how a customer accumulated their overall wealth and corroborates it with independent evidence rather than relying on self-declaration. It is central to managing high-net-worth, politically exposed and high-value-purchase relationships.

controls.name: Periodic and event-driven KYC refresh
controls.desc: Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.
aka: Enhanced due diligence and periodic KYC review

controls.name: Customer risk rating and classification
controls.desc: Assigns each customer a risk tier from factors such as customer type, sector, geography, products and channel, which then drives the depth of due diligence and monitoring. Consistent scoring focuses resources on higher-risk relationships.

controls.name: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
controls.desc: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.
aka: KYC refresh exit and restriction policy

controls.name: Dormant account reactivation controls
controls.desc: Alerts when an inactive account abruptly resumes activity and requires identity re-verification and updated due diligence before reactivation. Dormant accounts are attractive for takeover and for passing illicit funds.

controls.name: Signatory and mandate review
controls.desc: Identifies and verifies everyone holding signing, control or power-of-attorney rights over an account, and periodically reviews whether those powers remain justified. It reveals third parties who control accounts on behalf of others.

controls.name: Introducer and reliance due diligence
controls.desc: Assesses introducers and third parties on whom customer due diligence is relied, covering regulation, data access and file quality, backed by written agreements, per-introducer quality reporting and sample testing. It keeps outsourced onboarding to the institution's own standard.

controls.name: Additional checks for remote and higher-risk onboarding
controls.desc: Applies supplementary evidence, confirmation calls or direct contact when a customer is onboarded or instructed without meeting in person or presents other higher-risk characteristics. It compensates for the weaker assurance of remote channels.
aka: Additional checks for remote high-risk customers

controls.name: Agent and distribution network due diligence
controls.desc: Vets, trains, caps and monitors agents, sub-agents and distributors who onboard customers or move funds on the institution's behalf, including quality visits, outlier analysis and disclosure of principals. It limits control failures at the edge of a distribution network.

controls.name: Customer enquiry on unusual activity
controls.desc: Contacts the customer, or the relationship manager does so, to obtain and record an explanation of unusual transactions, relationships or recipients, and to test it against evidence. The answer informs whether activity is legitimate or should be escalated.

controls.name: Data quality and ownership controls
controls.desc: Measures completeness, accuracy and timeliness of the data that feeds screening and monitoring, reconciles sources and assigns named owners and deadlines for remediation. Controls built on poor data fail silently, so this keeps detection reliable.

controls.name: Privileged access and user-activity monitoring
controls.desc: Restricts and logs privileged and bulk access to customer and case systems and alerts on anomalous user activity. It deters insider misuse and leakage of sensitive investigations and customer data.

controls.name: Risk-based enhanced due diligence
controls.desc: Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.
aka: Enhanced due diligence and activity review

controls.name: Sector-tailored enhanced due diligence
controls.desc: Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.
aka: Enhanced due diligence on waste clients

controls.name: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
controls.desc: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.

controls.name: PEP enhanced measures
controls.desc: Applies corroborated source-of-wealth checks, senior sign-off, enhanced monitoring and sceptical review of public-sector links for politically exposed persons and their networks. It targets the corruption and misappropriation risk specific to these customers.
aka: Senior management approval and enhanced due diligence

controls.name: High-risk jurisdiction enhanced measures
controls.desc: Applies enhanced review, approval, limits and conditions to relationships or flows that involve jurisdictions rated higher risk for secrecy, corruption, conflict or weak controls. Triggers include nationality, residence, counterparties and payment routing.

controls.name: Merchant onboarding and business verification
controls.desc: Verifies merchant identity, business model, website content and expected volumes before activation and re-verifies on change, with remediation of weak merchants. It stops fronts and disguised businesses entering payment channels.

controls.name: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
controls.desc: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.
aka: Dynamic payment friction and tailored warnings

controls.name: Payee name verification
controls.desc: Checks the payee name against the destination account before release and warns on no-match or close-match, and flags payee-name mismatches against contracted entities. It interrupts misdirected, spoofed and fraudulent payments.

controls.name: Out-of-band call-back verification
controls.desc: Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.

controls.name: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
controls.desc: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.
aka: Hold or cooling-off on new high-value payees

controls.name: Risk-based transaction and account limits
controls.desc: Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.

controls.name: Strong authentication and step-up
controls.desc: Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.

controls.name: Customer education and awareness
controls.desc: Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.

controls.name: Trusted-contact and vulnerable-customer process
controls.desc: Allows customers to nominate a trusted contact and applies tailored handling and permitted escalation when vulnerability is flagged. It adds a safeguard for customers more exposed to manipulation or coercion.

controls.name: Seller, organiser and payee verification with payout controls
controls.desc: Verifies sellers, workers and fundraising organisers, matches payees to verified identities and holds or staggers payouts for new or anomalous accounts. It limits platform abuse.

controls.name: Segregation of duties and dual authorisation
controls.desc: Ensures no single person can create, approve and release a payment or master-data change, requiring an independent second approver. It controls insider and impersonation fraud.

controls.name: Vendor master-data and bank-detail change control
controls.desc: Requires independent verification and review of any new or changed supplier bank details before the next payment run, including challenge of redirections to third-country accounts. It stops payment-diversion and business-email-compromise fraud.

controls.name: Deposit holds and funds-availability policy
controls.desc: Places risk-based holds on uncleared or unusual inbound items and funds, limiting withdrawal until the item is confirmed good. It protects against losses from counterfeit, reversible or suspicious deposits.

controls.name: Cardholder authentication and tokenisation
controls.desc: Authenticates the cardholder at online checkout through an additional challenge and replaces stored card numbers with tokens. It blocks use of stolen card details and shifts liability for unauthorised transactions.

controls.name: Cheque and image analytics
controls.desc: Applies image and magnetic-ink analysis to deposited items to find alterations, counterfeits and duplicates, and monitors unusual deposit patterns. It stops paper-instrument fraud before funds are made available.

controls.name: Threat intelligence and takedown
controls.desc: Monitors for spoofed domains, fake apps, adverts, numbers and fraudulent campaigns, and arranges takedown, suspension and customer alerts. It removes criminal infrastructure.

controls.name: Consortium and external intelligence data
controls.desc: Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

controls.name: Income, affordability and underwriting verification
controls.desc: Independently verifies stated income, employment, obligations and application facts against third-party, bureau and prior-history data at origination. It reduces application, credit and insurance fraud.

controls.name: Claims analytics and payment verification
controls.desc: Scores claims, links parties, providers and addresses, monitors repeat claims by region or intermediary and verifies payee identity and sanctions exposure before settlement. It uncovers organised and repeat claims fraud.

controls.name: Independent verification of underlying transaction
controls.desc: Confirms the existence of underlying goods, services or receivables directly with the obligor or through inspection before funds are advanced. It defeats fictitious invoices and transactions that exist only on paper.

controls.name: Duplicate document and duplicate financing detection
controls.desc: Hashes and fuzzy-matches invoice and shipping documents within and across clients and checks shared registries so one asset cannot be financed twice. It detects reused and fabricated paper.

controls.name: Account detail change monitoring and cool-down
controls.desc: Contact, device or payee changes trigger notification to the prior channel and restrict risky actions for a short period, with alerts on clusters of changes. It disrupts takeover.
aka: Cooling period and notification on detail changes

controls.name: Refund destination and validation controls
controls.desc: Requires refunds, cancellations and aborted-deal repayments to go back only to the original payer and method after validation of the request. It blocks the use of refunds to convert illicit funds into clean payments.

controls.name: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
controls.desc: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.
aka: Corruption index in country risk model

controls.name: Three lines of defence accountability
controls.desc: Documents roles, ownership and escalation for first-line, compliance and independent assurance responsibilities for financial crime controls. Clear accountability reduces gaps and duplication.

controls.name: Management information and board challenge
controls.desc: Reports control performance indicators, backlogs and issues to senior management and the board on a regular cycle for challenge and decision. It keeps risk acceptance and resourcing visible.

controls.name: Enterprise and product risk assessment
controls.desc: Performs and refreshes a documented assessment of inherent risk, controls and residual risk across customers, products, channels, geographies and sectors, and links risks to specific controls and gaps. It directs resources and shapes policy.

controls.name: New product and change approval
controls.desc: Requires financial crime risk assessment and compliance approval before launching or materially changing products and features, with a post-launch review after a set period. It builds controls in before exposure arises.

controls.name: Scenario tuning and independent model validation
controls.desc: Periodically tests thresholds, coverage and segmentation, including above and below the line, and independently validates scenarios and models with documented rationale for changes. It keeps detection effective and defensible.

controls.name: Backlog management and surge resourcing
controls.desc: Tracks alert, review and case ageing against service levels, triages by risk and adds capacity or remediation programmes to clear backlogs. It prevents delay from eroding control effectiveness.

controls.name: Issue management and remediation validation
controls.desc: Records control issues with owners and deadlines, escalates overdue items and independently confirms that remediation has worked before closure. It ensures weaknesses are fixed rather than merely logged.

controls.name: Risk appetite and product policy statements
controls.desc: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.
aka: Risk appetite and product risk assessment

controls.name: Whistleblowing and speak-up channels
controls.desc: Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.

controls.name: Conflict-of-interest declaration and management
controls.desc: Requires declarations of conflicts from staff and third parties with annual refresh, rotation of relationship managers and challenge of exceptions. It reduces the chance that decisions are shaped by personal interest.

controls.name: Fair-treatment and de-risking safeguards
controls.desc: Documents that profile attributes alone are never grounds for adverse action and provides guidance supporting legitimate activity, such as humanitarian flows, instead of blanket exits. It limits unfair outcomes and bias in control design.

controls.name: Regulatory and typology intelligence updates
controls.desc: Tracks changes to regulation, disclosure regimes and national threat assessments and updates rules, location lists and procedures accordingly. It keeps controls aligned with the current threat.

controls.name: Sector and commodity risk policy
controls.desc: Sets internal risk guidance, acceptance limits and approval levels for sectors, commodities and fundraising channels exposed to elevated risk. It gives consistent decisions on how far to engage.

controls.name: Gifts, hospitality and expense controls
controls.desc: Requires logging, limits and pre-approval for gifts, hospitality and anything of value given to officials, with targeted audit of expenses and petty cash. It reduces improper inducements.

controls.name: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
controls.desc: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.
aka: Analyst review with documented rationale test

controls.name: Case management and cross-team escalation
controls.desc: Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.
aka: Case management and fraud MI governance

controls.name: Network case investigation
controls.desc: Investigates linked clusters and networks of accounts as one case, including broker networks and accounts connected to seizures or requests, rather than reviewing accounts individually. It disrupts organised activity that single-account review would miss.

controls.name: Law enforcement request handling and liaison
controls.desc: Handles law-enforcement, tax-authority and customs requests promptly, reviews related accounts and maintains rapid contact points. It supports investigations and asset recovery while keeping responses consistent.

controls.name: Information sharing and public-private partnership
controls.desc: Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

controls.name: Internal unusual-activity reporting channel
controls.desc: Provides a simple internal reporting channel and feedback loop so front-line staff can escalate observations, pressure and cash-handling anomalies. It turns staff observations into cases for review.

controls.name: Suspicious reporting timeliness and quality assurance
controls.desc: Measures how quickly suspicious activity reports are filed after suspicion forms and subjects narratives to peer or second-line review for completeness and usefulness. Weak or late reports are corrected and root causes fed back to analysts, so intelligence reaches authorities on time and in a usable form.

controls.name: Safeguarding and victim-centred referral protocol
controls.desc: Provides discreet escalation routes and private conversation procedures so staff can refer suspected victims of exploitation, coercion or trafficking to specialists, police and support organisations. It prioritises victim safety.

controls.name: Prior-report cross-reference and feedback loop
controls.desc: Checks parties against previously filed internal reports, links to reported accounts and feeds report outcomes back into tuning. It spots repeat subjects and sharpens detection.
aka: Network link analysis on prior reports

controls.name: Suspicion escalation and reporting decision protocol
controls.desc: Defines timelines, owners and criteria for escalating concerns and deciding whether to report, and for documents implying payments to proscribed groups. It ensures timely, accountable decisions.
aka: Escalation to financial intelligence unit decision

controls.name: Record retention and audit trail
controls.desc: Maintains records of identification, transactions, decisions and exceptions for the required period, with logs of deviations and a retrievable audit trail. It allows regulators and investigators to reconstruct events and supports later challenge of decisions.

controls.name: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
controls.desc: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

controls.name: Aggregated ownership and control assessment
controls.desc: Aggregates holdings of all designated persons, tests who really controls an entity despite formal shareholdings, and reviews recent ownership transfers and threshold proximity. It prevents ownership-based sanctions thresholds being avoided by splitting or nominee transfers.

controls.name: Embargoed-destination and geographic access restrictions
controls.desc: Blocks or refers transfers, goods, services and system access linked to embargoed or comprehensively sanctioned territories using address, route, payment-country and device-location signals. It prevents prohibited dealings from being processed.

controls.name: Sanctions escalation and legal clearance
controls.desc: Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.

controls.name: PEP, relative and close associate screening
controls.desc: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.
aka: PEP screening at onboarding and ongoing

controls.name: Sanctions and restricted-party screening
controls.desc: Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.
aka: Sanctions and watchlist screening including wallet addresses

controls.name: Payment message and free-text screening
controls.desc: Screens payment instructions, references and narrative fields for restricted parties, goods, places and concealment language using tuned matching logic. It catches exposure that does not appear in the customer record.
aka: Payment screening with tuned fuzzy logic

controls.name: Re-screening on list updates
controls.desc: Re-screens the customer base, linked parties and counterparties whenever sanctions or other lists change and on trigger events, with prompt list synchronisation. It closes the gap between onboarding checks and later designations.

controls.name: Adverse media and enforcement screening
controls.desc: Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

controls.name: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
controls.desc: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.

controls.name: Product-specific misuse surveillance
controls.desc: Monitors specialised products such as insurance, securities, safe deposit and prepaid instruments for surrender, free delivery, overpayment, assignment, matched trades and unusual access. It catches product-specific abuse.

controls.name: Lending and collateral integrity checks
controls.desc: Verifies lender ownership, loan terms and rationale, collateral origin and repayment sources, and alerts on early or third-party repayment. It prevents loans being used to place or layer funds.

controls.name: Gaming cash-out and win-document controls
controls.desc: Restricts cash-out and cheque issue to evidenced winnings, prohibits redemption to third parties and issues win certificates only on verified records, with periodic audit. It prevents gaming proceeds being used as a conduit for illicit funds.

controls.name: Gaming and betting play surveillance
controls.desc: Surveils chip transfers, buy-in versus play, low-risk or hedged betting, unusual stakes and collusive play between accounts or players. It detects use of gaming or betting products to launder or manipulate outcomes.

controls.name: Financial statement and tax reconciliation
controls.desc: Compares account flows with filed accounts, VAT or sales tax data and tax remittances, and links to VAT-fraud controls. It spots under-declared revenue and tax fraud proceeds.

controls.name: Tax residency self-certification testing
controls.desc: Tests customer tax self-certifications against indicia such as addresses and standing instructions, enforces collection of tax identification numbers and looks through passive entities to controlling persons. It limits misreporting under tax transparency regimes.

controls.name: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
controls.desc: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.

controls.name: Nested activity disclosure and detection
controls.desc: Requires respondents to disclose and approve downstream institutions and detects payment patterns that imply undeclared nested use. It limits exposure to unknown third-tier clients.

controls.name: Periodic respondent review and volume monitoring
controls.desc: Reviews respondent activity against expected volumes, updates expected activity and restricts routing via higher-risk banks. It keeps correspondent risk assessments current after onboarding.

controls.name: Request-for-information process
controls.desc: Sends requests for information to respondents or senders with deadlines, tracking of response quality and escalation of repeated deficiencies. It resolves unexplained activity and pressures partners to improve.

controls.name: Shell bank prohibition
controls.desc: Obtains and verifies attestations and checks registers to confirm counterparties are not shell banks lacking physical presence and supervision. It bars a high-risk category of relationship outright.

controls.name: Payable-through and sub-account controls
controls.desc: Restricts payable-through access or requires customer due diligence and monitoring at the sub-account holder level. It ensures third parties using a correspondent account are known and supervised.

controls.name: Payment message completeness and quality controls
controls.desc: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

controls.name: Cover payment transparency checks
controls.desc: Compares the serial payment message with the accompanying cover message so that originator, beneficiary and intermediary details can be checked for consistency. It stops parties being hidden by splitting a payment chain across messages.

controls.name: Third-party and intermediary due diligence
controls.desc: Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

controls.name: Vendor onboarding verification
controls.desc: Verifies new vendors and suppliers before first payment through registry checks, site or call validation and review against the existing vendor base. It prevents fictitious or controlled vendors being set up to extract funds.

controls.name: Ongoing third-party monitoring
controls.desc: Monitors business partners after onboarding for adverse media, ownership change, enforcement action and conduct concerns. It keeps third-party risk assessments current between formal reviews.

controls.name: Outsourcing and vendor oversight
controls.desc: Contracts service levels, quality standards and audit rights with vendors performing control activities, and samples their outputs for accuracy. It keeps outsourced screening, monitoring or onboarding to the institution's own standard.

controls.name: Licence and regulatory status verification
controls.desc: Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.

controls.name: Gatekeeper and company service provider due diligence
controls.desc: Assesses licensing, CDD standards and client mix of formation agents, lawyers and similar professionals and monitors formation volumes and concentration. It targets professional enablers.

controls.name: Omnibus and pooled account transparency
controls.desc: Secures contractual rights to underlying client information for intermediated or pooled accounts, requires look-through on request and monitors pooled flows against expected activity. It gives visibility of who is really transacting behind an aggregate account.

controls.name: Client money account verification and rules
controls.desc: Confirms legitimate client-account status and licensing and applies professional client-money rules, alerting on flows lacking a matter reference. It prevents professional accounts being used to move funds without underlying services.
aka: Professional body rules on client money

controls.name: Contractual compliance clauses
controls.desc: Writes compliance obligations into contracts, including representations, audit rights, termination rights for breach and minimum standards such as wage or disclosure terms. It gives the institution an enforceable lever over counterparties.

controls.name: Subcontractor transparency
controls.desc: Obliges counterparties to disclose and obtain approval for subcontractors, together with beneficial ownership details. It prevents work or funds being passed to undisclosed parties who would not pass due diligence.

controls.name: Labour provider and recruiter due diligence
controls.desc: Verifies licences, ownership, registration, tax compliance and wage-payment evidence of labour providers and recruiters at onboarding and review, and checks recruitment practices. It reduces exposure to exploitative labour supply and undeclared work.
aka: Enhanced due diligence for labour suppliers

controls.name: Trade document review and consistency checking
controls.desc: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.
aka: Trade document review by trained staff

controls.name: Price and value benchmarking
controls.desc: Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

controls.name: Shipment tracking and logistics evidence
controls.desc: Verifies that goods physically moved as documented by matching shipping, container, customs and logistics records, and by requesting transport evidence such as delivery confirmations and warehouse records for sampled trades. It exposes fictitious or misdescribed shipments used to justify payments.

controls.name: Route plausibility and transshipment screening
controls.desc: Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

controls.name: Free-zone and free-port due diligence
controls.desc: Applies enhanced checks to operators, counterparties, storage rationale and transactions that involve free-trade zones and free ports, including facility operator controls. It addresses the opacity and reduced oversight these locations can offer.

controls.name: End-use and outcome verification
controls.desc: Requires end-user statements, authenticates their signatories, verifies licences and sites, and obtains post-delivery reports for goods and funds. It confirms that goods or funds reach the stated end use.

controls.name: Re-export restrictions and undertakings
controls.desc: Obtains contractual and documentary undertakings restricting re-export or onward sale to specified destinations and flags rapid resale patterns. It limits diversion of goods to prohibited end users.

controls.name: Control-list and dual-use goods screening
controls.desc: Screens goods descriptions, HS codes and items against export-control, precursor and procurement watch lists, with access to technical review. It catches proliferation-sensitive and restricted goods.

controls.name: High-risk goods and commodity tagging
controls.desc: Maintains lists of higher-risk goods, species and commodity codes, tags relevant transactions and triggers extra documentary checks and screening of descriptions. It focuses scrutiny on the goods most associated with abuse.

controls.name: Trade amendment monitoring
controls.desc: Alerts on repeated or late amendments to consignee, destination, price or parties in a trade, and re-runs due diligence on changed parties. It detects manipulation of documents to evade controls after approval.

controls.name: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
controls.desc: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

controls.name: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
controls.desc: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

controls.name: Origin, provenance and chain-of-custody verification
controls.desc: Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

controls.name: Supply-chain mapping and traceability
controls.desc: Maps suppliers and sub-suppliers back through the chain, down to plot, mine or farm level where relevant, and requires traceability of key inputs to origin. It makes hidden high-risk sources visible so they can be excluded or audited.

controls.name: Supplier audit and remediation
controls.desc: Audits suppliers and processors, including interviews and records, and requires corrective action plans and remediation with support for affected workers. It verifies conditions on the ground and drives fixes rather than only detecting problems.

controls.name: Satellite and geospatial verification
controls.desc: Uses satellite imagery, land-cover and site evidence to test claims about operations, land use, production or activity at a location. It provides independent physical verification that does not rely on counterparty documents.

controls.name: Volume and capacity plausibility analytics
controls.desc: Compares reported volumes with capacity, production, mass balance, concession size and national trade statistics to test whether quantities are physically possible. It exposes inflated, laundered or mislabelled flows.

controls.name: Trade-and-settlement reconciliation
controls.desc: Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.

controls.name: Independent valuation and appraisal
controls.desc: Obtains independent valuations, appraisals or comparable-sale evidence for high-value assets, collateral and traded goods, and escalates large variances. It reveals deliberately mispriced assets used to move or conceal value.

controls.name: Asset registry cross-check
controls.desc: Cross-checks asset ownership, title history, security registrations and registry changes against official registers, including for changes close to designation or transaction dates. It confirms that the person presenting an asset genuinely owns it.

controls.name: Vessel due diligence and tracking analytics
controls.desc: Verifies vessel identity, ownership, flag history, insurance and class, and analyses tracking data for gaps, loitering, ship-to-ship transfers and spoofing. It addresses sanctions and illicit-trade evasion at sea.

controls.name: Credit and certificate registry verification
controls.desc: Verifies credit serial numbers, status and retirement on recognised registries, checks verifier accreditation, host-country accounting and independent quality ratings, and uses technical review of claims. It prevents double counting and fraudulent environmental credits.

controls.name: Role-based financial crime training
controls.desc: Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.

controls.name: Front-line recognition and conversation training
controls.desc: Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

controls.name: Typology-focused staff training
controls.desc: Briefs front-line, onboarding and investigation staff on current red flags, typologies and escalation routes, including sector-specific patterns and professional-enabler behaviours. It improves recognition of suspicious activity that rules alone cannot see.

controls.name: Analyst training on weak-signal combination
controls.desc: Teaches analysts to weigh several weak signals together, understand network and settlement structures, and avoid profiling on protected characteristics. It raises investigative quality and reduces both missed risk and unfair outcomes.
aka: Analyst training on weak signal combination

controls.name: Sector and partner awareness outreach
controls.desc: Educates retailers, suppliers, hospitality providers and other partners to recognise and report suspicious patterns, and invites reporting channels. It extends detection to people who see activity before the institution does.

controls.name: Velocity, volume and threshold rules
controls.desc: Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

controls.name: Structuring and threshold-avoidance detection
controls.desc: Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

controls.name: Cross-account and cross-channel activity aggregation
controls.desc: Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.

controls.name: Pass-through and rapid movement detection
controls.desc: Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

controls.name: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
controls.desc: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

controls.name: Profile-versus-activity deviation monitoring
controls.desc: Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

controls.name: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
controls.desc: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.

controls.name: Round-amount and repeated-value pattern detection
controls.desc: Alerts on repeated round-value or identical-value transactions by counterparty over a window. It is a supporting indicator of artificial, pre-arranged or structured flows and is best combined with other signals.

controls.name: Geographic and corridor-based monitoring
controls.desc: Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

controls.name: Third-party payer and depositor controls
controls.desc: Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

controls.name: Circular flow and round-tripping detection
controls.desc: Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

controls.name: Graph and network link analytics
controls.desc: Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

controls.name: Shared-identifier clustering and entity linkage
controls.desc: Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

controls.name: Successor and phoenix entity detection
controls.desc: Links newly formed companies to failed or abandoned predecessors through shared officers, addresses, customers and bank details. It detects serial use of disposable entities to shed liabilities and move value.

controls.name: Mule account detection model
controls.desc: Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

controls.name: Typology-based scenario design
controls.desc: Translates published and sanitised typologies and red flags into targeted monitoring scenarios and context-aware rules that are reviewed periodically. It aligns monitoring with known criminal methods.

controls.name: Risk-weighted counterparty monitoring
controls.desc: Weights alert priority by the assessed risk of the counterparty and profiles counterparties that cannot be explained by the customer's business. It directs analyst attention to payments involving higher-risk parties.

controls.name: Tightened monitoring for new accounts and entities
controls.desc: Applies lower thresholds and closer review during the first months of an account or entity and alerts on turnover far above onboarding projections. It addresses the elevated risk at the start of a relationship.

controls.name: Declared turnover and cash-flow reconciliation
controls.desc: Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.

controls.name: Payroll and worker payment flow analytics
controls.desc: Compares payroll flows with declared headcount, checks that wages reach workers' own accounts and flags cash payroll, recruiter payments and many-to-one wage patterns. It surfaces undeclared work and labour exploitation.

controls.name: Merchant transaction and portfolio monitoring
controls.desc: Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

controls.name: Public-funds payment monitoring and contract evidence
controls.desc: Flags credits from public bodies to personal or new accounts, atypical state-to-private flows and onward movement, and requires contracts and tender evidence for payments from state entities. It targets diversion of public money.

controls.name: Procurement bid and award analytics
controls.desc: Tests bidding and award data for rotation, cover bids, price clustering, splitting, variations and exceptions to competition, and requires independent cost and justification review. It detects collusion and corrupt awards.

controls.name: Intermediary payment and commission controls
controls.desc: Benchmarks agent commissions, rebates and fees, requires justification and compliance sign-off for payments in high-risk markets, and tests invoices for evidence of real services. It limits disguised bribery.

controls.name: Unlicensed money transfer detection
controls.desc: Detects remitter-like activity, pooled flows and informal channel use on accounts not authorised for money transfer. It finds unregistered MVTS operators and hawala-type settlement.

controls.name: Blockchain analytics and wallet attribution
controls.desc: Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

controls.name: Travel rule data exchange
controls.desc: Collects, validates and transmits required originator and beneficiary information with virtual asset transfers and holds or blocks transfers where counterparty data is missing or unreliable. It brings wire-like transparency to virtual asset payments.
aka: Travel rule data exchange and counterparty checks

controls.name: Obfuscation exposure and thresholds
controls.desc: Flags direct and indirect exposure to mixers, privacy services and obfuscation tools against defined thresholds and applies enhanced review. It manages the traceability loss these tools create.

controls.name: Unhosted wallet ownership proof
controls.desc: Requires proof of control, such as a signed message or small test transfer, before large transfers to or from privately held wallets are accepted. It confirms the customer owns the wallet and prevents use of third-party or hostile-controlled addresses.

controls.name: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
controls.desc: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.
